KEY MESSAGE 1....Record warmth this afternoon with a few gusty 
showers and thunderstorms possible this evening and again Friday.

Record breaking heat for some this afternoon. Preliminary data shows 
a new record likely at IAD of 88 degrees beating the old record of 
86 back in 1975. Records are also being challenged at DCA where 
temperatures 88 degrees was observed beating the old record 
of 87 back in 1975. Meanwhile, BWI hit 88 degrees beating the 
86 degree record from 1975. Mid to high level clouds along and 
north of I-70 combined with showers and even a few embedded 
t-storms over northeast MD have limited temperatures a bit 
compared to areas further south. This will likely limit any 
records at HGR and MRB this afternoon. See climate section below
for a list of today's record highs. 

The leading piece of shortwave energy continues to exit southeast PA 
and north-central MD early this afternoon while the cold front drops 
down out of southwest PA/southeast Ohio. The front looks to push 
toward western MD and the eastern WV mountains during the late 
afternoon commute before sinking down into northern VA and the 
Baltimore/DC metros this evening and into the overnight hours. 12z 
hi-res CAMS remain about the same in regards to timing (give or take 
and hour) and coverage with a general focus for thunderstorm 
coverage, mainly west of the Blue Ridge/US-15 and north of US-48/I-
66. 

Current timing puts convection over the western MD and eastern WV 
mountains between 21-00z/5-8pm before advancing south and east 
toward northern VA and the DC/Baltimore metros around 23-03/7-11pm. 
CAPE values will hover between 600-900 j/kg with 0-6 km bulk 
effective shear values around 35-45 kts mainly north of I-66/US-50. 
With that said, a Marginal Risk (Level 1 out of 5) for severe 
weather continues for locations west of US-15 and back into the 
western MD/eastern WV mountains. The greatest confidence for 
organized convection appears to be from Romney, WV/Cumberland, MD 
west to Oakland, MD and south toward Franklin, WV/Moorefield, WV. 
Elsewhere convection becomes a bit more isolated with more in the 
way of showers given the decrease in instability beyond the diurnal 
period along with downslope flow east of the mountains. Any 
storms that do form will have the capability of damaging winds 
and locally heavy rainfall. 

The front stalls near/south of the region Thursday morning as high 
pressure over southeast Ontario wedges down the mountains. This will 
return temperatures back into the mid to upper 60s under cloudy 
skies and on/off shower chances throughout the entirety of the day. 
The front retreats back to the north before washing out over the 
northern 2/3rds of the forecast area Thursday afternoon into 
Thursday night. This is due in part to the wedging high pressure 
system over southeast Ontario shifting toward the southern New 
England coast allowing winds to switch back to the southerly 
direction. The wedge will erode quickly as a result allowing for a 
quick spike in temperatures ahead of a stronger front Friday morning 
into Friday afternoon. 

Gusty showers and a few thunderstorms are possible Friday afternoon 
and evening (Marginal Risk (Level 1 out of 5) mainly east of US-15 
and toward the I-95 metros) as a true strong (Fall) cold front 
crosses the region. It will get breezy Friday afternoon as mid-level 
heights quickly fall and the surface pressure gradient tightens in 
response to a deepening low tracking to our north. Peak wind gusts 
of 35-45 mph are possible in the mountains, and 30-40 mph elsewhere. 
Wind Advisories may be needed for some portion of the Alleghenies 
and Blue Ridge Friday afternoon into Friday night although model 
trends continue to decrease winds over a large spatial area (i.e 
immediate surge along the front and disjointed trough compared to 
the pressure rises on the back end). A squeegee line of gusty 
showers and some thunderstorms are expected late Friday afternoon 
and evening ahead of the front. If thunderstorms can tap into the 
increasing winds aloft, there certainly could be a few strong to 
severe wind gusts.A potent upper trough passes through the region 
Friday night, bringing a reinforcing cold front that pushes out any 
lingering precipitation.

Highs Friday push into the upper 70s and low 80s early in the day 
before falling into 60s and 70s (40s and 50s mountains) Friday 
evening. Expect overnight lows in the 40s (30s mountains) Friday 
night. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Temperatures 10 to 15 degrees below average this 
weekend. Dry, but with areas of frost possible and near freezing 
temperatures, mainly west of I-95, Saturday night and Sunday night.

A strong mid-level disturbance will quickly transverse the region 
Saturday. High pressure will build into the region later Saturday 
through Tuesday. Gusty northwest and northerly winds will diminish 
through the day Saturday as the last of any precipitation moves out
